text: Here's Solid Light. The idea is simple: you draw one view, and Luma builds the other. You're working on the same little bridge, from two different angles. Let me show you.
I'll follow this little example. Pinch and hold, go around the ribbon, and bring it back to the start. Then release.
Now Luma's trying different depths. There's the bridge. That white line is the route it checked, and our little traveler can head across.
This time, I'll stop short. Luma can make the bridge wider, but it can't add length to my drawing. See those amber marks? That's the bit I need to connect.
So I'll extend the loop through the gap. Luma checks the new shape, finds a route, and we're across. We each changed our own part.

Let me show you the controls. You can pause, increase contrast, or reduce motion. And if a drawing goes wrong, you can clear it. Here, I've left the loop open. The dashed line shows the gap. Undo brings the earlier shape back.

The garden needs a roof as well as a path. I'll keep this lower loop, and draw a second loop around the upper guide. Each loop adds light. Now we've got shelter, with air underneath. We can choose a sturdier build, or use less light with the efficient option.

One more challenge: we've only got so much light. This shape goes over budget. I'll pull in the outer edges, keeping the crossing connected. There we go. After this, the workshop changes the span, the traveler's footprint, and the budget.

We built that together. My outline, Luma's tested depth, and a safe route home. Both contributions stay on display. Next opens the workshop. This is desktop footage; physical Quest testing is still pending.
